bottleneck: Rare-disease patients wait an average of five to seven years for a diagnosis, seeing multiple specialists while their condition progresses. Whole-exome and genome sequencing can end the odyssey, but access is uneven, insurance coverage inconsistent, and interpretation bottlenecks persist: most sequenced variants are of uncertain significance, and many causal variants hide in non-coding regions standard pipelines miss.
current_state: Rapid genome sequencing in NICUs proves diagnosis can take days, not years. Scaling that urgency to all undiagnosed patients is a systems, not a technology, problem.

sources.title: Gene therapies should be for all

title: Rare disease diagnostic odyssey still averages years
why_it_blocks: You cannot treat what you cannot name. Years of diagnostic delay mean missed therapeutic windows, irreversible damage, and families trapped in uncertainty while the technology to help them sits unused.
